subject: Control/data plane handoff — diagram gaps and handover checklist
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <engops@acme.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Nambiar <security@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Control/data plane handoff — initial diagram and gaps

Hi Soojin / Neha,

Thanks again for the headset demo last week. Attached is the boundary diagram our network team put together showing the proposed demarc between Acme-managed edge and Redwood control plane endpoints (acme-proposed-boundary-diagram.pdf). We want to make sure the control/data plane handshake is well-defined before the on-prem install window (target week of Aug 9).

Top concerns we want to validate:
- KMS traffic: where do KMS requests terminate and what networks are allowed (we need to satisfy our KMS attestations)
- Egress & NAT — will tenant data ever transit public egress or remain on private circuits?
- Control plane continuity in the event of edge loss — fallback model and observable signals

Can you confirm the right Redwood folks to walk these diagrams and propose a minimal evidence bundle for our security review? Ideally we get a short checklist and a remediation plan for diagram gaps.

Attachments: acme-proposed-boundary-diagram.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Engineering Operations
Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Control/data plane handoff — initial diagram and gaps

Alex — thanks for the diagram and callout. Looping Marcus and Kimberly to cover runtime and networking specifics.

Short response and proposed next steps:
1) Owners: Marcus will cover control-plane endpoints and routing; Kimberly will own egress/NAT and KMS flows; Neha will cover compliance evidence.
2) Immediate asks: can you send the edge NAT table and the proposed CIDR blocks for the tenant segments? That will let us validate ACLs and route maps.
3) Deliverable: we will produce a 1-page "handoff checklist" (I attached a working spreadsheet) and a change-marked diagram.

High-level gaps we see from first pass:
- KMS: need clarity whether Acme KMS endpoints must be called from inside the tenant VPC or via a dedicated egress path to your KMS. If the former, we need instructions for network peering and KMS ACLs.
- Control plane API endpoints: we recommend pinned FQDNs and an alias record for failover (we'll propose).
- Data plane replication: we need a short note on whether cross-rack replication uses private L2/L3 inside the colo or whether it will cross the internet.

I'll schedule a 30-minute diagram walk. Tentative: Mon Aug 2 10:00 PT — does that work for you?

Attachments: soojin-handoff-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

—
Soojin Lee

+1 to Soojin's checklist. A few inline technical notes (marked):

> KMS: need clarity whether Acme KMS endpoints must be called from inside the tenant VPC or via a dedicated egress path to your KMS.

If Acme requires calls from inside the tenant VPC, we'll need an outbound route from the runtime nodes into the Acme KMS CIDRs and a corresponding allow list. Alternative: a proxy in Acme edge that accepts requests over an mTLS channel (preferred). We can support either, but the ACLs differ.

> Control plane API endpoints: we recommend pinned FQDNs and an alias record for failover (we'll propose).

Marcus and I discussed: we will provide two stable FQDNs per control-plane cluster (primary + passive) and publish expected certificates. Expect to receive a small CSV of endpoints and IPs from us.

> Data plane replication: note on cross-rack replication path

We need the colo fabric L2/L3 plan. If replication crosses the Internet we will insist on encrypted tunnels between pods (WireGuard) and will recommend session-level encryption and per-tenant flow tagging.

Action items assigned:
- Kimberly: draft egress/KMS ACL matrix and recommend proxy pattern (due Jul 30)
- Marcus: export control-plane endpoint list and cert expectations (due Jul 30)
- Soojin: final handoff checklist and meeting agenda (due Jul 29)

Attachments: controlplane-endpoints.csv (CSV, 6 rows)

Kimberly Park
Network Security Lead
Redwood Inference
